f.title: Apply the Part C definition of adverse drug reaction
f.statement: In Part C, an adverse drug reaction means a noxious and unintended response to a drug which occurs at doses normally used or tested for the diagnosis, treatment or prevention of a disease or the modification of an organic function. This defines what is captured in annual summary reports, issue-related summary reports and case reports.
f.applicability: Part C of the Food and Drug Regulations (drugs), including C.01.016 to C.01.020 post-market reporting
f.processes: Reporting policy; Case processing & follow-up; Aggregate reporting

f.title: Apply the Part C definition of case report
f.statement: In Part C, a case report means a detailed record of all relevant data associated with the use of a drug in a subject. This is the content standard for case reports the manufacturer may be asked to submit (C.01.018(5), C.01.019(2)) and must keep (C.01.020).
f.applicability: Part C of the Food and Drug Regulations (drugs), including C.01.016 to C.01.020 post-market reporting
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Data integrity & records

f.title: Apply the Part C seriousness criteria (serious adverse drug reaction)
f.statement: In Part C, a serious adverse drug reaction means a noxious and unintended response to a drug that occurs at any dose and that requires in-patient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, causes congenital malformation, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, is life-threatening or results in death. This decides which reactions fall under the 15-day reporting duty in C.01.017.
f.applicability: Part C of the Food and Drug Regulations (drugs), including C.01.016 to C.01.020 post-market reporting
f.processes: Reporting policy; Medical review; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Assess expectedness against the label risk information (serious unexpected ADR)
f.statement: In Part C, a serious unexpected adverse drug reaction means a serious adverse drug reaction that is not identified in nature, severity or frequency in the risk information set out on the label of the drug. This decides which foreign serious ADRs must be reported within 15 days under C.01.017(b).
f.applicability: Part C of the Food and Drug Regulations (drugs), including C.01.016 to C.01.020 post-market reporting
f.processes: Reporting policy; Medical review; Safety labeling

f.title: Use the same serious ADR definition for the Food and Drugs Act
f.statement: For the purposes of the Food and Drugs Act (for example section 21.8, serious ADR information provided by prescribed health care institutions), serious adverse drug reaction has the same meaning as in subsection C.01.001(1).
f.applicability: Food and Drugs Act provisions that use the term serious adverse drug reaction
